sources.title: Decoupling and de Sitter Vacua in Approximate No-Scale Supergravities

evidence.text: Takagi factorisation of the complex symmetric supersymmetric mass tensor Z diagonalises the unperturbed X-sector Hessian. Its rescaled eigenvalues are (λi±|W|)², where λi are nonnegative singular values; large holomorphic Hessian entries therefore need not cause instability.

sources.title: Universal dS vacua in STU-models

evidence.text: Treat W and its derivatives through third order at the chosen point as independent complex variables. First derivatives fix SUSY breaking, second derivatives solve stationarity linearly, and third derivatives adjust the scalar mass matrix.

sources.title: De Sitter Vacua in No-Scale Supergravity

evidence.text: Transverse stability is studied using imaginary-component masses and the Hessian ∂²V/∂y_i∂y_j on the real slice. Quartic terms inside the Kähler logarithms alter this Hessian while preserving the real-slice potential.

sources.title: Decoupling and de Sitter Vacua in Approximate No-Scale Supergravities

evidence.text: The authors expand critical-point equations and the Hessian in ε, treating the three initially massless real modes as a degenerate sector and estimating mixing corrections perturbatively. Explicit STU families are constructed by solving inversely for fluxes at prescribed moduli values.

sources.title: Universal dS vacua in STU-models

evidence.text: For the near-supersymmetric construction, impose Vαβ=0 to pair scalar masses and combine stationarity with the geometric sGoldstino bound. Near no-scale points, the authors also construct examples without this pairing restriction.

sources.title: De Sitter Vacua in No-Scale Supergravity

evidence.text: The analysis uses the tree-level N=1 supergravity F-term potential expressed through G=K+ln W+ln W†. Substitution of monomial W reduces vanishing real-slice energy to an algebraic constraint on exponents.

sources.title: Cosmological attractors from α-scale supergravity

evidence.text: Which superpotentials yield Minkowski and constant dS/AdS potentials in no-scale supergravity, how do their pairings generalize geometrically to multiple fields, and how can matter and inflation be incorporated?

sources.title: From Minkowski to de Sitter vacua with various geometries

evidence.text: Can the construction of dS/AdS vacua from paired Minkowski superpotentials be extended to flat, compact, non-compact, and mixed Kähler geometries while breaking SUSY, stabilizing hidden-sector scalars, and generating observable-sector soft terms?

destination.title: Enlarging supergravity scalar potentials
destination.question: Which extensions of supergravity interactions generate useful scalar potentials, and what auxiliary-field and effective-theory restrictions accompany them?
destination.summary: Selected higher-derivative interactions provide one explicit route. The broader EFT-enlargement question also concerns inflation, de Sitter vacua and nonrenormalizable interactions, without establishing that it uses the same route.

regimes: Single-chiral examples with and without a superpotential
Explicit two-chiral examples without a superpotential
Broader EFT constructions known here only by description
assumptions: The higher-derivative terms are selected interactions, not arbitrary corrections
D-term uplift is an additional gauged-model mechanism
conventions: Higher-order terms in a Kähler potential are not automatically higher-derivative interactions
includes: Negative emergent contributions and competing D-terms
excludes: Generic ghost freedom for all higher-derivative supergravity
An inferred higher-derivative mechanism for every EFT-enlargement proposal
